summary: Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank demo for BrightLeaf Media. Showed embedding generation, vector search, and two-stage reranking flow (coarse recall -> rerank with cross-encoder style scoring). Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, dedicated vs hosted suitability for BrightLeaf's SLAs, and security concerns (SSO, audit logs, data retention). Agreed to run a pilot benchmark on 10k docs; next steps: pricing, security docs, sample data and benchmark results.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Sana Patel (BrightLeaf Head of Search), Liam O'Connor (Eng Manager), Maya R. (Data Scientist)
Recorded: yes

Summary (auto): Quick demo of hosted embeddings + rerank flow, Q&A on perf and security, agree pilot.

00:00:05 Avery: hey everyone thanks for joining, um i'm avery with redwood inference, i'll be owning the account. quick intros — diego is our solutions engineer, he'll demo the embeddings + rerank flow.
00:00:22 Sana: hi thanks, i'm sana, head of search at brightleaf. Liam and Maya are with me. we're trying to improve relevance for article search across content and user queries.
00:00:35 Liam: yeah looking for improvements over our current elastic setup, mostly precision at top K, and lower latency for interactive results.
00:00:48 Diego: cool, great context. quick agenda: 1) show hosted API embeddings + search pattern, 2) walk through rerank endpoint and cost/latency tradeoffs, 3) mapping to your pilot.

00:01:20 Diego: so here's a quick slide — we generate embeddings via a single API call, you can store vectors in your index (we integrate with typical vector DBs or you can use your own). Then a two-stage flow: recall with vector search then rerank with our rerank endpoint which re-scores top N docs using cross-attention scoring.
00:01:50 Maya: when you say rerank endpoint is that hosted or do we run inference ourselves?
00:01:55 Diego: hosted, it's part of our hosted api. you send the query plus candidate doc text and we return a score or a ranked list. it's optimized for short-batch scoring — think 10-100 candidates, low-latency path.

00:02:30 Avery: i'll pull up the console briefly — this is the api call patterns doc link i sent in the calendar invite (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-demo-deck).
00:02:48 Diego: demo time — i'm switching screens, heads-up there might be a bit of lag.

00:03:05 Diego: first code snippet: embedding generation. POST /v1/embeddings model=redwood-embedding-1 input=... returns 768-d vector. we showed batching and async upload patterns.
00:03:30 Sana: what's the throughput? we process ~2000 content ingests per hour during peaks.
00:03:38 Diego: hosted has autoscale; with our default profile you could expect ~500 embeddings/sec in a pooled setting for that model, but we can tune. for dedicated you'd get guaranteed throughput.

00:04:10 Diego: next we do recall with your vector DB — we showed an example using milvus/pinecone but you can use our built-in lightweight kNN cache. then the rerank call: POST /v1/rerank with query and candidates, returns scores. this path uses an optimized cross-encoder kernel.
00:04:45 Liam: how big are candidates? we normally send top 100 from elastic.
00:04:51 Diego: top 100 is okay but latency increases; typical production pattern is top 20-50 for interactive. you can do coarse recall of 100 then rerank top 20.

00:05:20 Maya: what about document size? our articles are 1k-2k tokens, sometimes longer.
00:05:28 Diego: for long docs we recommend chunking and storing chunk-level vectors; then rerank on candidate chunks or assemble context snippets. we have examples in the docs. chunking reduces tokens sent to rerank which helps cost/latency.

00:06:10 Sana: security questions — can you guarantee data residency and retention controls? we have EU-only data requirements for a portion of our corpus.
00:06:22 Avery: yes, hosted supports region pinning for data and compute; we also offer Private deployments for stricter residency or VPC options. for hosted specifically we support region selection and retention controls, and we have SOC2.
00:06:40 Liam: do you provide audit logs and SSO?
00:06:44 Avery: yes, SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs; also keys can integrate with customer KMS for private deployments. we'll share the security pack after the call.

00:07:15 Diego: demo time — i'm going to run a live example: query "best productivity tips" against a small article corpus. i'll show embedding vector generation then recall + rerank.
00:07:35 [screen share: terminal output]
00:07:50 Diego: POST embeddings -> vector returned in ~120ms for a single call, we batch later. then recall via pinecone (we mocked it in demo) returned top 50 in ~90ms. rerank endpoint with top 20 returned in ~220ms. so end-to-end interactive 400-600ms depending on network.
00:08:30 Sana: that's promising, our SLA target is under 600ms for query response in UI.
00:08:36 Diego: good match. note that for production we use continuous batching and prefix/KV cache which knocks down token compute on repeated sessions — that often drops p99s.

00:09:15 Liam: curious about cost — what's per-call price roughly for rerank?
00:09:20 Avery: pricing varies by model and token count; rerank is priced per request + per-token used. we'll send a pricing sheet, but ballpark hosted rerank per candidate scoring is cheaper than full cross-encoder runs on each doc because we optimize kernels and batch.

00:10:00 Maya: do you support function/tool-calling or structured output in rerank? we sometimes want category labels back.
00:10:08 Diego: the rerank endpoint returns scores but you can also call a structured scoring model or a small gpt-style model for labels in a follow-up stage; we have flexible endpoints.

00:10:45 Sana: example integration — we use elastic for text search, then vector plugin for dense recall, then a post-process step. any gotchas?
00:10:54 Diego: main gotcha is keeping embedding and rerank models in sync for semantic drift; we recommend version pinning and rollout policies (we expose model versioning). also monitoring quality with eval sets — Redwood Optimize can surface regressions.

00:11:30 Avery: speaking of Optimize, we can run a cost/perf sweep: try smaller embedding dims, quantized models for rerank, and tune top-k. Optimize gives recommendations.

00:12:00 Liam: for the pilot, what's a minimal scope you recommend?
00:12:06 Diego: recommend 1) 10k-50k doc corpus, 2) ~500 labeled queries for relevance evals, 3) two-week benchmark to measure p50/p95 latency and MAP@10. that gives a solid signal.

00:12:42 Sana: we can do 10k to start and provide the labeled queries.
00:12:47 Avery: perfect. we'll run a rerank benchmark and share results.

00:13:15 Diego: quick note on fallbacks — if capacity constrained we can route to a faster/smaller model variant though quality may vary. that's our graceful degradation.

00:13:40 [15-minute demo montage skipped for brevity in the transcript — live code + console walkthrough continues with examples of API calls, latency graphs, and a small benchmark run]

00:28:10 Diego: here's an example benchmark csv we run: queries, recall@k, rerank latency, tokens per rerank. in the demo i ran a 2k-doc toy set — results attached in the drive link.
00:28:42 Maya: i noticed some transcription errors in the earlier drive note, but the actual csv is clean.
00:28:50 Avery: we'll attach the exact benchmark run.

00:29:20 Liam: question: how do you handle PII — any redaction or masking options?
00:29:28 Avery: hosted is configurable for retention; we can redact sensitive fields on ingestion, or route those to private deployments if you need full control. we can discuss DLP patterns in the security call.

00:30:00 Sana: vendor comparison — we trialed OpenAI + Pinecone earlier; where does Redwood fit?
00:30:10 Avery: we position between managed api simplicity and dedicated inference economics — hosted gives easy integration; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and private gives data isolation. for search specifically we focus on production SLOs and tooling.

00:30:48 Maya: any known limitations for long docs and rerank scoring accuracy?
00:30:55 Diego: long docs need chunking; scoring accuracy depends on candidate quality. rerank excels when recall set has high recall. we provide eval tooling to help tune chunk size and recall thresholds.

00:31:30 Liam: compliance — what about SOC2 and ISO?
00:31:34 Avery: SOC2 Type II yes, ISO in progress — we'll share compliance pack (SOC2 report, penetration test summary, data flow diagrams).

00:32:05 Sana: ok timeline — we want pilot results in two weeks, and then evaluate pricing for full rollout.
00:32:12 Avery: we'll aim for that; diego will run the benchmark and i'll share pricing and security docs.

00:33:00 Diego: quick architecture note: if you want lower latency and dedicated throughput we recommend Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools with autoscaling. hosted is fine for smaller scale/fast ramp.

00:33:30 Maya: any gotchas integrating with our Elastic infra?
00:33:36 Diego: one is vector schema compatibility; another is sync latency for ingests — we recommend a pipeline that writes vectors on content creation and uses a background re-index for full-text. we have connector examples.

00:34:10 Avery: let's go over success criteria for the pilot: accuracy uplift over baseline (e.g., +X% MAP@10), p95 latency under 600ms, and cost per query within expected budget. do those sound right?
00:34:25 Sana: yes that'll work. also need audit logs for the pilot.

00:34:40 Avery: noted. we'll include audit logs in pilot.

00:35:05 Diego: demo continued — i toggled model variants to show quality differences; smaller model is ~40% faster but lost ~3 points MAP in this toy test. Optimize would recommend candidate sizes and model quantization.

00:36:00 Liam: do you support custom model hosting if we want to bring our own fine-tuned reranker?
00:36:07 Diego: yes for Dedicated and Private we support customer-provided models as long as they match supported formats; we can also host custom checkpoints in hosted for enterprise accounts under a vetted process.

00:36:45 Maya: okay for next steps can you send a checklist of data needed for the pilot?
00:36:50 Avery: yes — we'll send a data checklist: doc export (10k), labeled queries (500), current search logs, current infra notes.

00:37:20 Sana: what about rate-limiting and quotas — will the pilot have throttles?
00:37:26 Avery: pilot will have soft quotas but we'll set them to match expected traffic; for production we can set hard quotas and SLAs on Dedicated.

00:38:00 [small crosstalk — laugh]

00:38:20 Diego: security doc link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-security-pack (we'll share real pack after).

00:38:55 Liam: curious on observability — do you provide token-level cost breakdowns?
00:39:00 Avery: yes console has token-level breakdown, per-route dashboards, and trace hooks. Optimize surfaces cost tradeoffs.

00:39:35 Maya: will you run the benchmark on our data or do we run it?
00:39:40 Diego: we can run the bench if you provide data and credentials (S3 or upload). we'll do it as part of the pilot.

00:40:05 Sana: can we get the sample rerank latency numbers per region? we have users in EU and NA.
00:40:12 Avery: yes we'll include region-specific results. hosted allows region pinning. if you need EU-only we can arrange that.

00:40:45 Diego: little note on caching — prefix/KV cache reduces tokens on repeated sessions; for search it's particularly beneficial if users repeat similar queries.

00:41:20 Liam: any wildcards about uptime SLA?
00:41:24 Avery: Hosted has standard best-effort; Dedicated comes with SLA options (we'll include the SLA doc with terms).

00:41:50 Maya: what will you need from us to start the benchmark?
00:41:53 Avery: docs (10k), labeled queries (500), and an S3 or secure upload location + contact person.

00:42:20 Sana: timeline — we can get the labeled set by monday.
00:42:25 Avery: great. diego will reach out for credentials.

00:43:00 Diego: one more technical note — rerank endpoint supports batch scoring and streaming partial results for long candidate sets; choose streaming if you want early partial UX.

00:44:10 Avery: recap and next steps: 1) Avery send pricing + security pack, 2) Diego run rerank benchmark on provided 10k docs and share results, 3) Sana provide labeled queries and upload location, 4) schedule follow-up next week to review results.

00:44:45 Sana: sounds good. any blockers from our side? no.

00:45:10 Liam: small question — competitor lock-in concerns? our infra team worried about vendor lock if we rely on hosted.
00:45:20 Avery: valid concern. we provide export tools, model version pinning, and options for Dedicated/Private if you want to avoid lock-in. we emphasize portability.

00:46:00 Maya: last Q — data deletion policy for pilot?
00:46:05 Avery: we'll delete pilot data on request; we'll include retention and deletion details in the security docs.

00:46:40 Diego: demo wrap — i'll produce a benchmark report with raw csv and summary metrics.

00:47:05 Avery: i'll send next steps and target dates.

00:47:30 [small wrap-up chatter]

00:48:00 Sana: thanks a lot everyone.

00:48:05 Liam: thanks.

00:48:10 Maya: thanks.

00:48:20 Avery: thanks all — we'll follow up via email.

00:48:35 [recording ends on call platform at ~00:52:00 — some small post-call mute chatter not transcribed]
